question: True or false: Seneca's essay On the Shortness of Life argues that a human life is too short?
answer: False. Seneca argues the opposite: life is long enough if it is used well. What shortens it is postponement; he calls expectation the greatest obstacle to living, because it loses today waiting for tomorrow. People guard their money, he notes, and hand their hours to anyone who asks.
move: A title can state the complaint an author sets out to refute.
ask: Whose requests am I giving hours to that I would never give money to?
trap: True, taking the title for the thesis it argues against.
source: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life
reference: Seneca, Dialogues and Essays, trans. Davie, Oxford World's Classics, 2007
